summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Schopen earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (~1984–1991), UT Austin (~1991–1999), and UCLA (~1999–2019).

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at MSU Institute of Asian and African Studies and under George de Roerich, he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies and Moscow State University.

Gritli von Mitterwallner was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She completed her Dr. phil. (1964) and Habilitation (~1964–1971) at the University of Munich, where she later served as Professor from 1978 to 1991.
Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Thubten Chökyi Dorje, Terton Sogyal, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Guang Xing earned his PhD at SOAS, University of London (~1999–2002) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett. He became an assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong around 2003.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He worked as a researcher at the Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1986–2004), and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2004.
Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and was appointed professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima, a Buddhist studies figure, earned a law degree at the University of Tokyo and studied under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. He lectured at Toho Gakuin and founded Dogen Sangha International in 2007.

A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Bühnemann studied at Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner and with Michael Hahn. She held research posts in India and Japan before becoming a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral degrees at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann and held research posts attested in 2026 at Munich, Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Gunapala Dharmasiri worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1991 and 2008.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund specialized in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Stig Wikander and held an academic post at Uppsala University from around 1968 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University from ~1926 to 1933 and subsequently held a post there from ~1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun, active in Buddhist studies, studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, and trained under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. He served as abbot of Maha Bodhi Monastery in Singapore (attested 2013).
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University (~1997–2005) under Kenyo Mitomo. He also studied under Sheng Yen, Hoyo Watanabe, and several other teachers.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD at Columbia University. He taught religion at Columbia (1988–1999) and held the Kapany Chair in Sikh Studies at UC Santa Barbara (1999–2015).

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1893–1901). He held academic posts at Utrecht University (1924–1957) and the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944).

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, Hla Pe, and John Okell, and later served there as Senior Teaching Fellow (attested 2014).

Gustaf John Ramstedt specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1893–1902) and held positions at Helsinki (~1906–1941) and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1929).

Gustav Haloun was a sinologist who studied under August Conrady at Leipzig and completed his habilitation at Prague. He directed at Göttingen (1931–1938) and served as Chair of Chinese Language and History at Cambridge (1938–1951).
